newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans jailed for attack on black Britons.
newsitem.headline: Germans jailed for attack on black Britons.

text.p: Two German men were jailed on Monday for an attack on three black Britons last June which left one of the victims paralysed from the neck down.

A court in Potsdam near Berlin sentenced Mario Poetter, 24, and Sandro Ristau, 18, to eight and five years jail respectively for reckless driving and causing grievous bodily harm in a high-speed car chase which led to the Britons' car crashing.

Noel Martin, 36, from Birmingham, England, was paralysed when the car he and two other Britons were in hit a tree in the village of Mahlow, south of Berlin, after the Germans threw a rock through their rear window.
Poetter and Ristau admitted to shouting "nigger" at the construction workers at a train station before pursuing them, and then hurling a rock through the window.
The attack came during a wave of violence in eastern Germany last summer in which gangs of youths toting baseball bats and iron bars besieged a number of camp sites where foreigners were staying.

Eastern Germany, a region with high unemployment, has witnessed many high-profile attacks against foreign workers this year, reviving memories of a three-year wave of extremist violence after German unification in 1990.
Poetter and Ristau claimed the crash had occurred when the three Britons attempted to chase them after they had thrown the rock.
The two other British victims were Arthur Blackwood, age 39, from London and Mikel Ricketts, aged 38, from Middlesex.
Poetter and Ristau told police that they mixed with local neo-Nazi circles in Mahlow, but denied belonging to any organised racist group.
Judge Klaus Przybilla had told the court during the trial that the case might be serious enough to warrant a conviction for attempted murder, but in the event decided that this could not be proved.
Two weeks ago an 18-year-old German went on trial for the murder of another British building worker, Lee Hawthorn, in September 1994.
The young man, identified only as Steffen H., is accused of tying Hawthorn to his car and dragging him over eight km (five miles) behind the car.
